content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem's causal chain, starting with the symptom that account page requests failed, citing the relevant error logs and the rise in error rate from baseline to peak during the incident, before moving into the underlying cause.

Tracing deeper, the requests were throwing a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py starting at 14:20, which traces back to the monthly-spend-feature flag being enabled for most evaluations around 14:21, routing traffic through the faulty code path. I'm working through whether this flag toggle was the sole production change in the window, checking the change records to confirm no deploys or earlier changes occurred that could also explain the onset, and figuring out how to properly phrase that deploys were ruled out due to absence of any other changes in the record.

I'm also ruling out shopper disconnects as a cause — those ClientDisconnected errors were present at baseline before the onset and didn't change in frequency after 14:20, so they look pre-existing rather than new. The remaining gap is why the code path actually divides by zero once the flag is on — I don't have direct evidence pointing to the source of the zero denominator, but the causal chain so far is that enabling the flag routed account page requests into code that raises a division by zero.

For mitigation, the flag revert at T18 took about 22 seconds to clear before the incident was marked resolved, which lines up with the metrics window rather than instant recovery. I'm also noting the rollout pattern — the flag seems to have ramped partially before going fully on, consistent with a percentage-based rollout rather than an all-at-once switch.

For contributing factors, I'm flagging two: first, the flag change went to all traffic within a minute with no staged rollout or error-rate guard, so I'd recommend adding a gradual rollout with automatic halt on error spikes. Second, there was no test exercising the account page with the monthly-spend-feature flag on, which would have caught the division-by-zero at spend_summary.py:47 — so the fix should guard against a zero denominator there and add a corresponding test before re-enabling the flag.

Now I'm also considering that nobody was paged since the alert wasn't linked to on-call, meaning Argus caught it but resolution came through human noticing rather than automatic escalation — this points to a detection/process gap, and the action should be routing HighErrorRate alerts to page on-call directly.

I'm also folding in whether the flag change by an admin without monitoring the error rate deserves its own factor, but I'll fold that into the alert-routing issue rather than add a fourth item. And I should capture the actual fix as an action: resolve the division-by-zero bug at spend_summary.py:47 before re-enabling monthly-spend-feature, while noting the flag is already off so that part doesn't need a separate action.

For the "went well" section, I'm noting that Argus correctly pinpointed the onset and identified the flag change as the triggering event, forming candidate C1 around the timing of the alert, and that the mitigation agent reverted the flag shortly after the alert fired.

For "went wrong," I want to avoid duplicating the paging gap since that's already a contributing factor. I'm weighing whether the incident being closed by a human before Argus confirmed the revert actually lowered the error rate is a legitimate gap — the metrics window hadn't caught up yet when the status was checked, so there's no verified confirmation the fix worked. I think it's fair to note this as a limitation of process rather than a hypothesis being tested.

There's nothing clear for "got lucky," so I'll leave that empty. For "still at risk," the division-by-zero bug at spend_summary.py:47 is still live in the code, meaning re-enabling the monthly-spend feature would likely reproduce the same account page failures.

For assumptions, I'm noting that the flag change is only suspected as the cause, not confirmed, and the revert's effect wasn't directly verified. I'm also assuming the ZeroDivisionError logs correspond to the failed requests shown in the error rate, and that the account-page error series reflects those failures within the broader request alert.

For root cause, the monthly-spend-feature flag routed account page requests through a code path in spend_summary.py that divides by zero at line 47, triggering the errors.

For cause in plain words: turning on the new monthly-spend feature made the account page run a calculation that divided by zero, causing those pages to fail. I'm tracking the timeline of when the flag was read by each record to confirm there was just one flag change in the sequence.

Ruling out other causes: no deploys occurred besides the flag toggle itself, and client disconnects happened before onset so they're unrelated. There's no earlier change in the record to consider, so nothing else needs ruling out.

For action items, I'm noting the fix should handle the zero divisor at spend_summary.py:47 and add a test rendering the account page with the monthly-spend feature enabled.

The remaining items: roll out the monthly-spend-feature flag change on io-shop in staged increments with an error-rate check that halts rollout (prevent), and link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call paging route (detect). Now I'll write it up.

action_items.item: Fix the division at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 so the account page handles a zero divisor, before monthly-spend-feature is switched on again.
Add a test that renders the account page with monthly-spend-feature on and covers the case that hit the division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47.
Roll out io-shop flag changes, monthly-spend-feature included, in stages, with an error-rate check that halts the rollout and reverts the flag when errors rise.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to the on-call paging rotation.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The service's share of failed requests rose from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_while_broken} while it was broken, and peaked at {errors_at_worst}. The account page error rate was highest at {Gbac1.7}.
Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. These errors were logged from {G5309.3} and were not seen in the half hour before.

From the onset, monthly-spend-feature evaluated on for most requests and then for all of them, which sent account page requests down the code path that holds that division. Before {G971b.6} every evaluation was off. At {G971b.6} it was off {G971b.1} and on {G971b.2}, and every evaluation after that was on.

ruled_out.what: A deploy or release: the change query for the day before the onset returned only the flag toggle and no deploys, and all replicas run a single revision.
Shoppers disconnecting: ClientDisconnected errors were logged in the half hour before the onset while account pages rendered normally, and none were logged after it.

causal_chain.step: The flag was on because admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. The flag provider's history shows this as the one flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour before.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Turning on a new monthly-spend feature made the account page run a calculation that divided by zero, so those pages failed to load.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag change reached all account page traffic within about a minute. No staged rollout and no error-rate check that halts a flag change were seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout with an automatic halt would have kept the failure to a small share of shoppers and switched the flag back as soon as errors rose.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test or pre-production check was seen that ran the account page with monthly-spend-feature on, which could have caught the division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 before the flag went on in production.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been found before shoppers reached it, and the flag would not have been switched on until it was fixed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to an on-call incident, so nobody was paged when it fired.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: An on-call engineer would have been engaged as soon as the alert fired, rather than depending on someone happening to watch the Argus UI.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well: The error logs named the exact file and line of the failure, src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, which tied the failure straight to the newly enabled code path.
The Investigator named the flag toggle as the leading candidate {T13.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature back off {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, and that change can be undone.

input.root_cause: Switching monthly-spend-feature on sent account page requests down a code path that divides by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. Those requests raised ZeroDivisionError and failed instead of rendering. The record does not show why the divisor was zero.
input.still_at_risk: The code that divides by zero is still behind monthly-spend-feature, so switching the flag back on could make account pages fail again.
input.symptom: Account pages failed to load for many shoppers
